replies.description: how the session writes replies: terse bans the words a, an, the, is, are, was and were; tight drops preamble, recap and filler; standard keeps full prose

rules.terse: Replies are terse: chat prose only, in the user's language. In chat prose, lists and numbered steps included, never write a, an or the, and never write is, are, was or were; fragments, `→` for leads to and `=` for is are fine. Example: "The hook is not reading the setting, so the reminder never fires." becomes "Hook not reading setting → reminder never fires." Code, commands, paths, identifiers, error text, numbers and every not, no, only and except stay whole. Full sentences return only for a security warning, a confirmation before an irreversible action and a question to the user; a label such as `Warning:` on anything else does not lift the ban. Commits, PR text, docs, code comments and saved files keep normal prose. A lone `?` from the user asks for the previous reply in full. The output style sets the layout; this sets how dense the words are.
rules.tight: Replies are tight: no preamble, recap, filler or hedging. Code, commands, paths, identifiers, error text, numbers, warnings and every not, no, only and except stay whole, and a security warning or a confirmation before an irreversible action is written in full sentences. The output style sets the layout; this sets how dense the words are.
rules.standard: Replies are standard: full prose. The output style sets the layout; this sets how dense the words are.

budget.description: high: medium, except the deep branch review, the design critique and the hardest work get the model and effort of their high kinds, set on each Agent call. medium: every agent dispatch uses the model its kind resolves to in lib/model-kinds.json. low: an agent whose kind resolves to a tier named under budgets in lib/model-kinds.json dispatches on that tier's replacement instead, except the hardest work, which keeps its model at medium effort. The old names full, normal and lean still read as high, medium and low

rules.high: Budget is high, so exo asks you to set these Agent call parameters. When you dispatch exo:critique-ui or the deep review (exo:review-branch on a `REVIEWER:` line that prints a model), set the call's `model` to `{model:review-deep-high}` and `effort` to `{effort:review-deep-high}`. When you dispatch exo:solve-hard, set its `model` to `{model:hardest-high}` and `effort` to `{effort:hardest-high}`. These two values replace the agent's and the `REVIEWER:` line's; set no other dispatch's `model` or `effort`.
rules.low: Budget is low, so exo asks you to set these Agent call parameters. When you dispatch exo:critique-ui or the deep review (exo:review-branch on a `REVIEWER:` line that prints a model), set the call's `model` to `{model:review-deep@low}` and `effort` to `{effort:review-deep}`. When you dispatch exo:solve-hard, set its `model` to `{model:hardest-low}` and `effort` to `{effort:hardest-low}`. These replace the agent's and the `REVIEWER:` line's values. When the Agent tool dispatches any other plugin agent whose kind in lib/model-kinds.json resolves to model {from} (the kind is the agent's entry under agents, looked up under kinds, whose tier the provider named at the top maps to a model under providers), set {to} as the Agent call's own `model` instead.

codexRules.high: Budget is high: spawn exo-critique-ui-high in place of exo-critique-ui, exo-solve-hard-high in place of exo-solve-hard, and exo-review-branch-deep-high for a `REVIEWER:` line that prints a model, each with the same prompt.
codexRules.medium: Budget is medium: when a `REVIEWER:` line prints a model, spawn exo-review-branch-deep for that review, with the same prompt.
codexRules.low: Budget is low: spawn exo-critique-ui-low in place of exo-critique-ui, exo-solve-hard-low in place of exo-solve-hard, and exo-review-branch-deep-low for a `REVIEWER:` line that prints a model, each with the same prompt.
